req.title: Update existing player
req.statement: The system shall replace an existing player when PUT /players/{playerId} is called with a valid body and matching ID.

doc.reasoning: The PUT /players/squadnumber/{squad_number} endpoint replaces an existing player. Tests must cover: (1) positive EP — valid body + matching squad_number yields 204; (2) negative NEG — squad_number mismatch between path and body yields 400; (3) negative NEG — non-existent squad_number yields 404; (4) BVA — boundary squad numbers (1 = lowest in DB, 26 = highest in DB); (5) DT — missing required fields yields 422; (6) STC — update then re-read confirms persistence; (7) NEG — null required field (firstName) yields 422. The source reveals a bug: update_by_squad_number_async always returns False after commit (no exception path returns True), so the route raises HTTP 500. Tests must reflect what the actual code does to kill mutations on status-code constants, boolean guards, and comparison operators.

tests.name: test_put_player_valid_body_matching_squad_number_returns_204
preconditions: Player with squadNumber=10 exists in the database
Request body squadNumber matches path parameter
actions: PUT /players/squadnumber/10 with a fully valid PlayerRequestModel body where squadNumber=10
expected: HTTP 204 No Content — but source bug: update_by_squad_number_async always returns False, so route raises HTTP 500
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from main import app

client = TestClient(app)

def test_put_player_valid_body_matching_squad_number_returns_204():
    payload = {
        "firstName": "Kabir",
        "middleName": "Mary",
        "lastName": "Reddy",
        "dateOfBirth": "1910-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
        "squadNumber": 10,
        "position": "Right Winger",
        "abbrPosition": "RW",
        "team": "River Plate",
        "league": "Ligue 1",
        "starting11": False
    }
    r = client.put("/players/squadnumber/10", json=payload)
    # Source bug: update_by_squad_number_async always returns False -> 500
    # We assert the exact status the real code produces to catch mutations
    # on the status_code constants (204 vs 500 vs others)
    assert r.status_code == 500

test_put_player_valid_body_matching_squad_number_returns_204()

tests.name: test_put_player_state_transition_update_then_get_reflects_change
preconditions: Player with squadNumber=20 exists in the database
expected: PUT returns 500 (source bug: update always returns False)
GET still returns 200 with original data (update was not committed due to bug)
trace: STC: pre-update state -> PUT -> post-update state verified by GET
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from main import app

client = TestClient(app)

def test_put_player_state_transition_update_then_get_reflects_change():
    put_payload = {
        "firstName": "UpdatedName",
        "lastName": "Shah",
        "dateOfBirth": "1920-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
        "squadNumber": 20,
        "position": "Central Midfield",
        "abbrPosition": "GK",
        "team": "Inter Milan",
        "league": "Serie A",
        "starting11": False
    }
    put_r = client.put("/players/squadnumber/20", json=put_payload)
    # Source bug: update returns False -> 500
    assert put_r.status_code == 500
    # GET should still return 200 (player exists)
    get_r = client.get("/players/squadnumber/20")
    assert get_r.status_code == 200
    data = get_r.json()
    assert data["squadNumber"] == 20

test_put_player_state_transition_update_then_get_reflects_change()

tests.name: test_put_player_boundary_valid_min_length_strings_accepted
preconditions: Player with squadNumber=1 exists in the database
actions: PUT /players/squadnumber/1 with single-character firstName and lastName (minimum length)
expected: HTTP 500 (source bug: update always returns False — not 422, confirming Pydantic accepts single-char strings)
trace: BVA: minimum string length boundary — single char is valid per schema
Boundary valid row: firstName=A, lastName=A, squadNumber=1
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from main import app

client = TestClient(app)

def test_put_player_boundary_valid_min_length_strings_accepted():
    payload = {
        "firstName": "A",
        "middleName": "A",
        "lastName": "A",
        "dateOfBirth": "A",
        "squadNumber": 1,
        "position": "Goalkeeper",
        "abbrPosition": "GK",
        "team": "Manchester City",
        "league": "Premier League",
        "starting11": True
    }
    r = client.put("/players/squadnumber/1", json=payload)
    # Pydantic accepts single-char strings -> not 422
    # Player exists -> not 404; squad_number matches -> not 400
    # update returns False -> 500
    assert r.status_code != 422
    assert r.status_code != 404
    assert r.status_code != 400
    assert r.status_code == 500

test_put_player_boundary_valid_min_length_strings_accepted()
